question: A project manager pastes her internal meeting notes into the chat and asks for the weekly client update. The notes include unreleased pricing and a blunt remark about the client's own team. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) The update may come back shorter than usual, since the notes cover only what was raised in that one meeting.
B) Material she supplied only as background may surface in the client-facing draft and be sent before anyone notices.
C) The notes may be too long for one message, so part of the week's discussion is left out of the client update.
D) The update may adopt a tone that is far too casual for the client, because her meeting notes were written casually.
correct_answers: B) Material she supplied only as background may surface in the client-facing draft and be sent before anyone notices.
explanations: A shorter update is a quality concern she would spot immediately, not a consequence that reaches the client unnoticed.

Correct. Everything pasted is treated as material available for the task unless the request says otherwise. Unreleased pricing and a candid internal remark are exactly the content that must be marked as background only, or removed before pasting.
A set of meeting notes sits comfortably within a single message, and omissions from length are not what makes this situation hazardous.
Tone drift is real but visible on a first read, and it is corrected with one instruction about register.
